title: Ukrainian Borscht with Beef, Beetroot and Cabbage
summary: A hearty ruby-red soup of tender beef, beetroot, cabbage and potatoes in a rich meat broth, brightened with lemon and fresh dill. A spoonful of soured cream on top is essential.
equipment: large casserole or stockpot (at least 7 litres) with a lid

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck, trimmed and cut in half
large carrot, cut into 2-3 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt
waxy or all-purpose potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm pieces
green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
raw beetroot, peeled and coarsely grated
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh dill, chopped, plus extra to serve
lemon juice, plus extra to serve

steps.title: Make the broth
steps.text: Put the beef, halved onion, carrot chunks, bay leaves, 0.5 tsp salt and 2400 ml water in the casserole and bring to the boil over high heat. Lower to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for about 2 hours, skimming off any foam, until the beef pulls apart easily with a fork. Slow, gentle cooking melts the tough connective tissue in chuck, which gives both tender meat and a full-bodied broth.

steps.title: Prepare the beef
steps.text: Lift the beef onto a board and discard the onion, carrot and bay leaves. Once it is cool enough to handle, cut or pull the meat into bite-size pieces. Skim the fat from the broth and set 120 ml of it aside for the vegetables.

steps.title: Cook potatoes and cabbage
steps.text: Bring the remaining broth back to the boil, add the potatoes, cabbage and 0.75 tsp salt, then cover and simmer gently for 8-10 minutes until the potatoes are just tender. The potatoes should still hold their shape, as they will cook a little more later.

steps.title: Build the beetroot base
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat and soften the chopped onion for about 5 minutes. Add the beetroot, grated carrots and 0.5 tsp salt and cook, stirring, for 3-5 minutes. Stir in the tomato purée for 1-2 minutes until it darkens, then add the reserved 120 ml broth and scrape the pan. Frying the tomato purée concentrates its savoury flavour and helps fix the bright colour of the beetroot.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.text: Stir the beetroot mixture and the beef into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes, until the soup is deep red and piping hot. A short simmer lets the flavours mingle without dulling the colour.

steps.title: Brighten and serve
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the dill and lemon juice, then taste and add a little more lemon if you like it sharper. Serve with a spoonful of soured cream and extra dill. The acid balances the sweetness of the beetroot and keeps its colour vivid.

tips: Wear gloves or rub your hands with a little oil before grating beetroot to avoid pink-stained fingers.
A common mistake is boiling the soup hard after the beetroot goes in, which turns it brownish; keep it at a gentle simmer.
Borscht tastes even better the next day, once the flavours have settled.
Use the large holes of the box grater so the beetroot and carrot keep a little texture.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months (without the soured cream). Reheat until piping hot (74 °C) and add a squeeze of lemon to refresh the colour. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
